newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH JAN-SEPT FOREIGN DIRECT INVESTMENT $972.4MLN.
newsitem.headline: CZECH JAN-SEPT FOREIGN DIRECT INVESTMENT $972.4MLN.

text.p: Foreign direct investment (FDI) into the Czech Republic totalled $972.4 million in the first nine months of 1996, the Czech National Bank said on Thursday.
That compares with nine-month FDI in 1995 of $1.984 billion which included the $1.32 billion equity expansion by a Dutch-Swiss consortium in SPT Telecom a.s.
In a statement, the central bank said that total FDI inflow in the post-Communist period since 1990 was $6.7 billion.

The largest volume of investment for the first nine months of 1996 came from the Netherlands which made 25.1 percent of the total, followed by the United States (23.9 percent) and Germany (20.3 percent).

For the post-Communist period Germany led all foreign direct investment into the country, accounting for 28.6 percent of the total, followed by the Netherlands with 15.3 percent and the United States with 15.1 percent.

Investment was highest in the transport and communications sector where 23.6 percent of the total was made, while 15.9 percent of the investment was made in transportation equipment and the automotive industry.
